plan: The dominant strategy in this auction game is to bid your value, which is $20. This strategy maximizes expected profit because it balances the risk of overbidding and paying more than the item's worth against underbidding and losing the auction when the item is worth more. Since this is the only round, there are no previous rounds to consider for adjusting strategy. Thus, I will bid exactly my value of $20 to ensure the best long-term expected outcome.

The dominant strategy in this auction game is to bid my private value, which is $29. This strategy maximizes expected profit by ensuring that I win the item whenever the value exceeds the second-highest bid. Since values are independently redrawn each round and there is no history to consider, I will follow the dominant strategy and bid $29 to maximize my profit in the long run.

The dominant strategy in this auction game is to bid exactly my private value for the prize, which is $45. This strategy maximizes expected profit because if I win, I gain the difference between my value and the second-highest bid. Bidding higher risks overpaying, while bidding lower risks losing the auction when it would have been profitable to win. Given no history, I will adhere to the dominant strategy.
